claims.text: The proposed Mg-Ti-V-Zr alloy will have a density below 6 g/cm³.
An 850 °C/30 min hold followed by 900 °C/60 min will produce a dense, single-phase-like microstructure.
The two-step protocol suppresses elemental volatility while promoting solid-state diffusion.
The two-step protocol will improve oxidation and corrosion barrier properties relative to standard isothermal sintering.
High-energy ball milling under argon ensures powder homogeneity and reduces elemental segregation.
Holding at 850 °C for 30 min initiates diffusion without significant volatility.
Holding at 900 °C for 60 min achieves full densification while maintaining phase stability.
The two-step thermal profile facilitates chemical short-range order.
The two-step thermal profile suppresses grain-boundary segregation.
The 850 °C step minimizes Mg and volatile transition-metal loss while enabling nucleation of a stable solid solution.
The 900 °C step promotes grain growth and pore elimination without excessive volatility or phase decomposition.
Reduced volatility and phase decomposition lead to a homogeneous microstructure with enhanced barrier properties.
The proposed process will yield a relative density above 95%.
The proposed process will yield an FCC or BCC solid solution containing less than 5% secondary phases.
The proposed process will reduce oxidation rate by 50% relative to isothermal sintering at 950 °C.
The proposed process will improve corrosion resistance by 40% in 3.5% NaCl solution.
Standard isothermal sintering at 950 °C for 60 min yields 88% relative density, significant Mg loss, and a segregated multiphase microstructure.
Below 820 °C, relative density falls below 90% because diffusion is insufficient.
Above 980 °C, Mg loss exceeds 5%.
A dwell longer than 90 min at 900 °C causes Mg loss above 5%.

contradictions.description: The proposed optimum is a sequential 850 °C/30 min plus 900 °C/60 min treatment, but the falsification experiment tests separate 60 min isothermal treatments at 850, 900, and 950 °C. It therefore does not directly test the proposed two-step protocol against the baseline.
The intervention states that the 900 °C step achieves 'full densification,' whereas the quantified prediction only requires relative density above 95%; these are not necessarily equivalent.
